snippet.title: Why America's Power Grid Is at Risk of Blackouts
snippet.description:
Flipping a light switch is one of those things you only notice when it doesn't work — and Americans have had the luxury of not noticing for about a century. That streak is why it's worth paying attention when the normally sedate bureaucrats who oversee the power grid start telling Congress that the red lights are flashing. Here's what they're actually worried about. 

In 2025, roughly 60% of Spain's electricity supply dropped off the grid in about five seconds, leaving parts of four countries dark for 10 hours. American regulators warn we aren't immune. 

In 2026, the North American Electric Reliability Corporation projected that nearly half the U.S. population faces high risk of rolling blackouts within a few years. PJM — the country's largest grid operator, serving 65 million customers — expects to lose about 40 gigawatts of capacity to plant retirements by 2030, and to replace it with, at best, a little over 30. 

Why the gap? Grid operators buy whatever power is cheapest, rebidding as often as every five minutes. Wind and solar are cheap when they run — subsidies sometimes let their prices go negative — but in 2024 wind only generated power about a third of the time and solar less than a quarter.  

The result? A country in which more and more of our electricity comes from sources that are simply unavailable for long stretches of time.

snippet.title: How to smoke a brisket
snippet.description:
Haven’t done a brisket video in a while, so here is my go-to method for perfect brisket, every time.
 
1. Take your time trimming the brisket. Remove any pieces that are sticking out or are super thin. They will just overcook. When removing the fat, remove a little a time. You can always remove more, but you can’t add back. The goal is to get the brisket as even as possible, so it cooks evenly.

2. I like to use yellow mustard as the binder and my AP rub with more course ground black pepper. Whatever seasoning you use, go heavy with it and season both sides AND the edges. You can do this a few hours before smoking and let it rest at room temperature.

3. For temperature monitoring, I like using the RFX from @thermoworks . It is very accurate, has a great range and gives you all the info right on your phone.

4. Preheat your smoker to 225 degrees and place the brisket fat side down. This is my method for pellet cookers. If you use a different smoker, you might want to cook fat side up. Try both and see what works best for you.

5. Smoke until it reaches 160-170 degrees internal temperature AND the bark is nice and dark. Place it in a foil pan, still fat side down, add a little beef tallow and beef stock to the pan. I started using this method after seeing @kendrick_bbq do it and it’s been a game changer. Perfect briskets on the pellet smoker every time!

6. Wrap the foil pan and place it back on the smoker, bump the temp to 250 and continue cooking until probe tender.

7. That can be anywhere between 200-210 degrees. I like to start checking around the 200-degree mark. You temperature probe should go in without any resistance, like a hot knife in butter. If it feels firm, continue cooking and repeat in 20 minutes.

8. When the brisket is done, remove it from the smoker, remove the foil from the pan and rest it for an hour. You can do it in your oven that’s turned off or a room temperature cooler. Anything that will retain heat.

9. Slice and enjoy!!!

snippet.title: 해외에서 화제라는 한국의 인프라 마비
snippet.description:
"전국 전력망은 최고인데, 사무실에 두꺼비를 키운다고?"
한국 지사로 발령받아 근무하게 된 한 외국인이 사무실에서 겪은 어이없고 황당한 정전 사건을 고백했습니다.
한국은 워낙 전력 인프라가 탄탄해 정전 따위는 감히 상상도 하지 못했지만, 어느 날 아침 사무실 전체가 갑자기 암흑으로 변했습니다.
당황한 팀장님이 "두꺼비집이 내려갔다"고 말하자, 외국인은 '누가 사무실에서 두꺼비를 키우나' 싶어 경악했습니다.
알고 보니 쌀쌀해진 날씨에 직원들이 자리마다 켜둔 미니 난로 때문에 누전차단기가 내려간 것이었습니다.
국가 전력망은 레전드 수준인데, 미니 난로 몇 대에 속수무책으로 무너지는 오피스 인프라(?)의 반전 귀여움을 영상으로 확인해 보세요.

snippet.title: Doomsday Prepping for Optimists
snippet.description:
Support my work, buy me a coffee. https://ko-fi.com/thequietpart

In a time of rising tension, the impulse to prepare for the worst calls louder than ever. This is an act of complying in advance that must be resisted. In this video I examine the idea of "Doomsday Prepping" in pursuit of learning how it is preppers turn fear into practice such that us optimists on the other side can do the same with our hope.

Chapters:
0:00 The Global Polycrisis
1:33 Doomsday Preppers
6:24 Solarpunk Optimism
8:04 The Reality of Dystopia ft. Palantir
9:03 An Introduction to Prefigurative Politics
15:05 A real example of Mutual Aid as Prefiguration
19:33 What can Optimists learn from Doomsday Preppers?
23:30 The Quiet Part 

This video has been a long time in the making, and represents the culminations of so much of my own learning since I started this small YouTube channel. It centers in on a theory for political engagement that grounds itself in doing real things, right now, here in real life. I yearn for a better, more sustainable, and more just Solarpunk future. But, even I feel that same instinct to look at all that is happening right now in the world. It makes you want to bury your head in the sand and turn your back on the world. Which is something I myself am no stranger to. 

But, what if... instead of turning away..? We turned towards each other. What if the optimists of the world took our ideas as seriously as doomsday preppers. What if we lace up our boots, and focus on practicing for a better future, instead of the apocalypse?

The main book I reference: 

Raekstad, P., & Gradin, S. S. (2020). Prefigurative politics: Building Tomorrow Today. Polity Press. 

Throughout the video I use different screenshots of headlines, all of which are real, and taken from different popular sources. You can just search them up. I didn't use them for their content so I'm not citing them as sources since that wasn't the point of my using them, all I wanted was to highlight how their titles tell a story. Regarding mentions of things related to Palantir, I have many videos on that you can check out. 

https://youtu.be/t-D3lCenGKs?si=-ouVjLHNu2f76Nrt

https://youtu.be/DvGAOinicxQ?si=P6J5-4xxW_SRiR9v

https://youtu.be/g47nhEFR3Os?si=II7PwTqab1asbp9b

(Also you should like, like this video, and share it around. I am certain it's not particularly algorithm friendly).


Edit: At 13:18 I was supposed to flash up a definition, but instead I accidentally showed that screenshot about how Officials representing the State of Israel essentially agreed that they're committing warcrimes. Rather than fix that error, I'll just laugh and leave it as-is for emphasis.  Fuck genocide, free Palestine.

snippet.title: #Doomsday Prepping
snippet.description:
I started a #MarvelMarathon just so I could figure out what the heck my boys were talking about. 😂

And honestly, I wanted to know what was so exciting about Avengers: Doomsday coming out in December!

Well, 30+ movies and a couple of series later, I can honestly say I’m SO glad I decided to do this.

A few unexpected bonuses I never saw coming…

❤️ My boys actually come hang out with me! I have sons of all ages, and when I turn on a Marvel movie, they often shut off their computers and video games to come watch with me. Even my son who’s away at college gets in on it because we’ll talk about the movies over the phone.

❤️ The conversations! Every morning on the drive to school, my youngest son and I have the best conversations about everything MCU. We talk about our favorite characters, theories, and what’s going to happen next. His favorite is Spider-Man, of course. 🕷️

❤️ I’m actually hooked! Who knew?! I love how all the movies and storylines connect. And don’t even get me started on the Easter eggs and those end-credit scenes! Now I’m the one looking for clues. 😂

What started as me just trying to understand my boys has turned into one of my favorite ways to spend time with them.

And the best part? It’s been such a simple, inexpensive way to make memories together.

Now we’re all counting down to Avengers: Doomsday in December!

Marvel fans, who’s your favorite MCU character? Mine is in the comments.
